items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: has contributed music for films by Woody Allen and Martin Scorcese

ctx.x: Vince Giordano was born on March 11, 1952 in Brooklyn. He directs the Nighthawks, where he switches between string bass, tuba and bass saxophone, and offers the occasional vocal. He has become the premier performer of 1920s and 30s jazz and popular music and has contributed music for films by Woody Allen and Martin Scorcese.
Vince was interviewed in New York City on January 11, 2007 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
